author: A.Arizón
html:
The null can never be justified in any circumstance. It either represents a future value or an non-existent one, and so it must be marked by compiler as either a “future” or a constant “not apply”. It was a programming mistake inherited from the first compilers in 1950’s.
Tomy Hoare, null’s invertor, has explained it a million times and he warns (nearly pledges) not to use it, neither to justify it in any circumstance or scenario.

A programmer can decide at random what a nulls means inside his brain and convince itself about its proper use.
Unfortunately, neither the compiler, not any consumer of the nullable code will agree with that “mental meaning” is because nulls bears no information at all.

Its use is neither appropriate in functional programming, not in imperative one or in any future programming paradigm.

The keyword null got its place by a chain of errors. Just let kill it and forget about that nightmare.
